concepts.name: Circuit moth
concepts.description: A moth turns the idea of an evolving design into a living silhouette. Routed wings and paired eye spots bring hardware and scrutiny into the same image.
concepts.tradeoff: Strong for a brand emblem and stickers; the wing pattern needs simplification for a tiny icon.
concepts.alt: Ivory engraved moth with circuit-patterned wings on warm black.
concepts.research: Original metaphor informed by circuit routing and the use of pictorial symbols in technical identities.
concepts.idea: Draw a magnificent original moth with wings spread, seen straight from above, strong bilateral structure but organic natural wing edges. The forewings contain beautifully organized chip-floorplan rectangles and curved traces that transition into engraved moth veins. Two large oval wing eye-spots suggest attentive verification, not actual detached eyeballs. The hindwings are delicately scalloped, antennae graceful, segmented narrow body. Combine fine scientific natural-history engraving with substantial bold black-and-ivory woodcut shapes, not an outline-only tech icon. Highly designed purposeful wing pattern, not a random PCB texture. Creature should look elegant, intelligent and a little mysterious. No halo or enclosure.

concepts.name: Wafer iris
concepts.description: An engraved eye looks through a wafer-like iris. Its nested patterns make inspection and careful measurement the visual idea.
concepts.tradeoff: The eye is memorable, though it can suggest monitoring if used without Verity context.
concepts.alt: Engraved eye with a geometric wafer-patterned iris and delicate radial lines.
concepts.research: Inspired by ASML optical metrology, where measured patterns reveal alignment and focus.
concepts.idea: Create one sophisticated large almond-shaped human eye emblem with an extraordinary circular iris: precise interlocking rectangular wafer-die tessellation arranged inside the iris, framed by elegant engraved radial fibers. A dark pupil with a tiny simple ivory square reflection at its upper right. Outer eyelids are expressive clean bold tapered curves, not realistic skin, no face, no eyelashes. Lower curved contour has three concentric metrology-like fine arcs. The eye should feel like a finely engraved optical instrument plate blended with a contemporary editorial illustration, cerebral and beautiful. Distinct from IBM eye pictogram: much more circular mechanical iris detail, no horizontal stripe motif, no letters or bee. No creepy surveillance camera, no occult triangle.

concepts.name: Signal heron
concepts.description: A heron folds a precise, patient posture into a sculptural emblem. Its wing feathers become ordered signal paths.
concepts.tradeoff: A broader metaphor for precision, with a less literal chip connection.
concepts.alt: Sculptural ivory heron with circuit-like wing feathers, curved neck and long beak.
concepts.research: An original animal metaphor using ordered routing paths as the feather structure.
concepts.idea: Draw a graceful heron in a distinctive compact almost-circular resting posture, long slender S-curved neck, sharp beak angled down toward its own raised folded wing, one visible long leg subtly tucked. The broad folded wing is the visual focus: four to six elegant nested feather bands become purposeful right-angle signal traces toward their ends, each ending with a tiny square terminal. Combine precise engraved ornithological illustration with mid-century woodcut silhouette design. Organic curved body and neck contrasted with architectural feather routing, sophisticated calm intelligence and patience. Not a crane lifting equipment, not a phoenix, no flames, no enclosing circle. No random cybernetic gadgets.

concepts.name: Lithography bloom
concepts.description: Layered petals unfold from a patterned center, turning the fabrication process into a botanical illustration.
concepts.tradeoff: Best suited to expressive brand artwork rather than a literal hardware symbol.
concepts.alt: Ivory sculptural flower with geometric patterned petals and a precise engraved center.
concepts.research: A metaphor for the repeated patterned layers in photolithography, not a claim about a real fabrication structure.
concepts.idea: Invent an exquisite botanical-mechanical bloom, seen in three-quarter view, a sculptural lotus-like flower made of six to eight thin folded ivory petals. Each petal has an engraved rectangular lithography pattern that follows the folded plane, part botanical vein part precise photomask. Petals radiate from a small dark square seed chamber with a delicate grid of ivory dots. Fine crosshatching and a few confident filled ivory planes create depth without gradients, like an elegant scientific copperplate engraving reinterpreted for a contemporary technology brand. One short curved stem supports it. Show all petal silhouettes cleanly. Intricate but disciplined, beauty in the relationship between living form and manufactured layers. No actual colored flower, no decorative leaves or butterflies.

concepts.name: Bond weaver
concepts.description: Two carefully drawn hands guide fine connections into a tiny die. It gives the engineering process a human, crafted character.
concepts.tradeoff: A narrative illustration with more detail than a compact app icon.
concepts.alt: Two engraved hands weaving fine bond wires around a small exposed silicon die.
concepts.research: An original craft metaphor informed by fine interconnects and the relationship between people and machines in identity design.
concepts.idea: Create an evocative compact editorial emblem of two beautifully drawn human hands working together around one small exposed rectangular silicon die. One hand enters from upper left with thumb and forefinger holding a fine curved wire, the other rises from lower right guiding a second wire. Seven or eight graceful parallel bond-wire arcs connect tiny die pads to a subtle open support ring, like a tiny loom. Hands are anatomically correct and elegant, not robotic, no extra fingers; the gesture should be clear and readable. Fine etched linework and strong ivory shapes, with restrained crosshatching. A feeling of a master craftsperson carefully weaving logical connections, not holding a generic square CPU badge. No sleeve details, no tools, no background, no text.

concepts.name: Silicon strata
concepts.description: An exploded stack reveals routing, structure and a central core. It makes the hidden layers of a chip feel tangible.
concepts.tradeoff: A strong hero illustration; its layered perspective will need a separate small emblem.
concepts.alt: Exploded isometric silicon layers with etched routing patterns and a suspended central core.
concepts.research: Inspired by patterned layers in chip fabrication and physical-design floorplan imagery.
concepts.idea: Draw a dramatic compact exploded axonometric silicon structure as a finely engraved architectural illustration. Four thin irregular square-like layers float above one another, each rotated only slightly and sharing one precise vertical axis. Top layer has a bold geometric circuit-floorplan labyrinth with large clear regions; lower layers reveal an elegant web of routed paths, a crystalline inner core and ordered square contacts. A tiny solid faceted central core is suspended in the gap between the middle layers, the focal point. Fine vertical guide lines only where useful, strong negative-space air between layers, no surrounding box or pin-border chip icon. Warm ivory line engraving and subtle crosshatched grey planes on black. Scientific architectural drama, no futuristic city, no colored neon, no glossy rendered cube.
